updates.scope_and_remaining_work: The actual arbitrary-division-ring Wedderburn-Artin existence theorem is now integrated at its semisimple-ring scope. The finite-algebra radical quotient is proved semisimple and its actual decomposition is constructed. These depend on proved pinned Mathlib results, not a custom existence axiom. Compatible finite module decompositions are separately constructed in ProductPresentation and SemisimpleExistence.

The actual left regular module is explicitly equivalent to its natural columns, then to the displayed finite direct sum of natural-module copies over arbitrary division rings. Coordinate ring homomorphisms define the inflated actions, other factors act by zero, and positive-dimensional natural factors are proved simple. No transpose-as-ring-map or commutative-scalar shortcut is used. Finite products for the inner repeated copies are the canonical finite direct-sum model.

The full nonsplit formula for actual division-ring matrix/product modules is proved from row-space lower bounds and coordinate-row generators, then transported through the displayed actual ring and compatible module equivalences. The public semisimple existence theorem constructs BOTH presentations internally, by mapping finite simple summands to actual natural factors through nonzero column projections and Schur’s lemma. The arbitrary Artinian radical-top and finite-dimensional-algebra clauses use the existing literal module top. No decomposition, multiplicity or seed-rank equality is supplied to the final existence theorem. Positive matrix sizes are retained. Empty products and zero modules give zero. This is a noncomputable existence/correctness development, not an executable Wedderburn algorithm.

The split multiplicity formula is proved for the literal module top. The exact printed variant, which supplies a split decomposition of the ORIGINAL ring and the original-ring action on M/JM, has its own wrapper. A separate variant handles a supplied split decomposition of A/J. Scalar restriction from A/J to A preserves the canonical quotient generator rank. Algebraic closure is unnecessary once the displayed split decomposition is supplied, so this proves a stronger statement at the recorded scope. It does not claim an executable splitting/decomposition procedure.

For every division ring and positive matrix size, the natural module has canonical seed rank one and every nonzero vector generates. The proof uses entries w_i / v_j with the inverse on the correct right side. The positive-size convention of the surrounding natural-simple-module discussion is essential: size zero has seed rank zero. This guard remains explicit in Lean and is tested, not silently discarded.

For arbitrary division rings and positive block size, the actual shared matrix action on m natural-module copies has canonical rank ceil(m/d). The rectangular-matrix, natural-column-product and finite-direct-sum formulations are connected by actual module equivalences. Zero multiplicity is included. This is not the independent-factor action, whose bound is a maximum across distinct factors.
